# @ratmath/linalg

> Exact rational linear algebra with fast float previews that sharpen to exact answers. Part of the RatMath Shelf; numbers come from @ratmath/core (a peer dependency). ESM: `import * as linalg from "@ratmath/linalg"`.

Built from 0.1.0, commit 77cf842. `file:line` is relative to the package root (also node_modules/@ratmath/linalg/); on GitHub: https://github.com/ratmath/linalg/blob/77cf842/<file>#L<line>. Docs pages are under https://ratmath.com/linalg/. Full types: index.d.ts. `(Q ⇒ E)` is a Refinement: `.quick.value` is the float preview Q at once, `.exact()` the exact E.

Types: `type Entry = number | bigint | string | Rational | Integer | { numerator: bigint; denominator: bigint }`; `type MatrixInput = Matrix | Entry[][] | Entry[]`; `type Trust = "good" | "rough" | "unsure"`; `type Algebraic = AlgebraicReal | ComplexAlgebraic`; `type AlgebraicMatrix = Algebraic[][]`; `type NormKind = 1 | 2 | "inf" | "fro"`

## Docs

- https://ratmath.com/linalg/llms-full.txt: every page below as Markdown, each with a runnable example
- Pages: index (Introduction), reference (Reference), fast-exact (Fast, then exact), elimination (Elimination and solving), subspaces (The four subspaces), determinants (Determinants), inverses (Inverses and fast exact solving), eigen (Eigenvalues and eigenvectors), jordan (Jordan and canonical forms), orthogonality (Orthogonality and least squares), factorizations (Factorizations and powers), integer (Integer matrices), exponential (The matrix exponential), matrix-functions (Matrix functions), nonlinear (Nonlinear solving), iterative (Iterative and eigenvalue methods), fields (Other number systems)

- `lu(A: MatrixInput) → ({ perm: number[]; L: number[][]; U: number[][] } ⇒ { perm: number[]; L: Matrix; U: Matrix })` — PA = LU. · src/ops2.js:222 · factorizations
- `ldl(A: MatrixInput) → ({ L: number[][]; D: number[]; positiveDefinite: boolean } ⇒ { L: Matrix; D: Rational[]; positiveDefinite: boolean } | null)` — Symmetric A = L·D·Lᵀ (no square roots, so exact). · src/ops2.js:234 · factorizations
- `qr(A: MatrixInput) → ({ Q: number[][]; R: number[][] } | null ⇒ { Q: Matrix; R: Matrix; normsSquared: Rational[] })` — QR. · src/ops2.js:273 · orthogonality
- `gramSchmidt(A: MatrixInput) → (number[][] | null ⇒ Matrix[])` — Orthogonal basis (exact, not normalised) of the span of the columns, zero columns dropped. · src/ops2.js:285 · reference
- `power(A: MatrixInput, k: number | bigint) → (number[][] | null ⇒ Matrix | null)` — A^k for any integer k (negative uses the inverse; null if singular). · src/ops2.js:304 · factorizations
- `trace(A: MatrixInput) → Rational` — Trace, exact and immediate. · src/ops2.js:339
- `pseudoinverse(A: MatrixInput) → (number[][] ⇒ Matrix)` — Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse A⁺, exact (it is rational for rational A). · src/ops2.js:365 · orthogonality
- `leastSquares(A: MatrixInput, b: MatrixInput) → ({ x: number[][]; residual: number[][] } ⇒ { x: Matrix; residual: Matrix })` — Least squares: the x minimising ‖A·x − b‖ (the one of least norm when there are many). · src/ops2.js:389 · orthogonality
- `spaces(A: MatrixInput) → { rank: number; nullity: number; columnSpace: Matrix[]; rowSpace: Matrix[] }` — Bases for the column space (pivot columns of A) and row space (nonzero rows of rref). · src/ops2.js:420 · subspaces
- `hermite(A: MatrixInput) → { H: Matrix; U: Matrix; pivots: number[] }` — Hermite normal form: { H, U, pivots } with U·A = H, U unimodular. · src/ops2.js:437 · integer
- `smith(A: MatrixInput) → { S: Matrix; U: Matrix; V: Matrix; diagonal: bigint[] }` — Smith normal form: { S, U, V, diagonal } with U·A·V = S, d₁ | d₂ | …. · src/ops2.js:443 · integer

- `jordan: typeof similarity` — Jordan form: same as similarity(A), kept as its own name. · src/ops2.js:593 · jordan
- `expm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — exp(A). · src/ops2.js:599 · exponential
- `sinm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — sin(A): every entry as a certified interval. · src/ops2.js:644 · matrix-functions
- `cosm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — cos(A): every entry as a certified interval narrower than 2^-bits. · src/ops2.js:639 · matrix-functions
- `sinhm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — sinh(A) = (exp(A) − exp(−A))/2. · src/ops2.js:655
- `coshm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — cosh(A) = (exp(A) + exp(−A))/2. · src/ops2.js:649
- `sqrtm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] | null ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — The principal square root: the one matrix X with X² = A whose eigenvalues all have positive real part. · src/ops2.js:666 · matrix-functions
- `logm(A: MatrixInput, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] | null ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — The principal logarithm: the one X with exp(X) = A whose eigenvalues have imaginary part strictly between −π and π. · src/ops2.js:682 · matrix-functions
- `powm(A: MatrixInput, t: Entry, options?: { bits?: number }) → (number[][] | null ⇒ RationalInterval[][])` — A^t for a rational t, as exp(t·log A) with the principal logarithm. · src/ops2.js:693 · matrix-functions
- `norm(A: MatrixInput, p?: NormKind) → (number ⇒ Algebraic)` — A matrix norm, exactly: p = 1 (largest column sum) and "inf" (largest row sum) are rationals, "fro" is the square root of a rational, and 2 is the largest… · src/extended.js:200 · inverses
- `cond(A: MatrixInput, p?: NormKind) → (number | null ⇒ Algebraic | number)` — The condition number ‖A‖·‖A⁻¹‖ in the same norms, exactly. · src/extended.js:215 · inverses
- `definiteness(A: MatrixInput) → (null ⇒ Definiteness)` — Definiteness of a symmetric matrix from the signs of its eigenvalues: { kind, positive, negative, zero } with kind "positive-definite",… · src/extended.js:273 · eigen
- `cholesky(A: MatrixInput) → ({ L: number[][] } | null ⇒ { L: AlgebraicMatrix; D: Rational[] } | null)` — Cholesky factorization A = L·Lᵀ of a symmetric positive definite matrix, with exact square roots. · src/extended.js:301 · factorizations
- `symmetricEigen(A: MatrixInput) → (null ⇒ { values: Algebraic[]; Q: AlgebraicMatrix })` — Orthogonal diagonalization of a symmetric matrix: A = Q·diag(values)·Qᵀ with QᵀQ = I, exactly. · src/extended.js:367 · eigen
- `integerKernel(A: MatrixInput) → Matrix` — A basis of the integer solutions of A·x = 0, as the columns of a Matrix (LLL-reduced, so the vectors are short). · src/extended.js:417 · integer
- `integerImage(A: MatrixInput) → Matrix` — A basis of the lattice spanned by the columns of A (all integer combinations of them), as the columns of a Matrix, LLL-reduced. · src/extended.js:432
- `lllReduce(A: MatrixInput) → Matrix` — LLL-reduce a lattice basis given as the rows of an integer matrix: short, nearly orthogonal rows spanning the same lattice. · src/extended.js:441 · integer
- `eigenspace(pairs: [bigint, bigint][][], value: Algebraic) → AlgebraicVector[]` — A basis of the eigenspace of an irrational or complex eigenvalue, as vectors with entries in Q(λ) (polynomials in λ). · src/extended.js:75
- `jordanAlgebraic(pairs: [bigint, bigint][][], eigen: unknown) → { J: AlgebraicMatrix; P: AlgebraicMatrix } | null` — J and P with A·P = P·J when some eigenvalue is irrational or complex. · src/extended.js:127
- `complexField: FieldOps<Algebraic>` — Exact algebraic numbers, real or complex, as a field for the functions in `field`. · src/extended.js:453 · fields
- `algebraicMatrix(rows: (Entry | Algebraic)[][]) → AlgebraicMatrix` — Rows of exact numbers from rationals ("3/4", 2, 5n), Core Rationals, or algebraic numbers already built. · src/extended.js:465 · fields
- `numberFieldOps(K: unknown) → FieldOps<any>` — The operations of a NumberField as the plain record field.js works with. · src/extended.js:29
- `AlgebraicReal class: poly, lo, hi, rational, refine, isRational, interval, toRational, toNumber, toString` · from @ratmath/algebraic/poly · eigen
- `ComplexAlgebraic class: poly, conjugate, refine, box, toNumbers, toString` · from @ratmath/algebraic/complex · reference
- `AlgebraicVector class: lambda, toStrings, approximate, toNumbers` — An exact eigenvector whose entries are polynomials in λ (degree below that of λ's polynomial), i.e. an element of Q(λ)ⁿ. · src/structure.js:194 · reference

## Namespaces

- `poly` (src/poly.js): charpolyPairs, charpolyMod, charpolyModular, everything from @ratmath/algebraic/poly
- `interval` (src/interval.js): everything from @ratmath/algebraic/interval
- `teach` (src/teach/index.js): fmt, gaussJordan, solveSystem, inverse, determinantByElimination, cofactorExpansion, bareiss, modularDeterminant, guessAndCheck, gramSchmidt, lu, leastSquares, eigen, sturmWalk, newtonKrawczyk, powerBySquaring, jordanBlocks, exponentialSeries, fourSubspaces, dixonLifting, WALKTHROUGHS, RowReducer, gcd, lcm
- `methods` (src/methods.js): exactDouble, jacobi, gaussSeidel, sor, conjugateGradient, powerMethod, inverseIteration, qrAlgorithm, pivoting
- `exact` (src/exact.js): run, integerRows, bareiss, rrefPairs, determinantBareiss, solvePairs, nullBasis, inversePairs, prime, invMod, detMod, hadamardBits, determinantModular, provablyNonsingular, gcd
- `float` (src/float.js): rrefFloat, detFloat, inverseFloat, solveFloat, guessRational
- `field` (src/field.js): rref, det, transpose, multiply, identity, inverse, rationalField, intervalField, algebraicField, primeField, galoisField, isProbablePrime, NumberField
- `algebraic` (src/algebraic.js): everything from @ratmath/algebraic

## Example

```js
import { det, solve, eigenvalues, teach } from "@ratmath/linalg";
const job = solve([[2, 1, 1], [1, 3, 2], [1, 0, 0]], [4, 5, 6]);
console.log("float preview:", job.quick.value.x);
console.log("exact:", job.exact().x.toStrings());
console.log("det:", det([["1/2", "1/3"], ["1/4", "1/5"]]).exact());
console.log("golden ratio:", eigenvalues([[1, 1], [1, 0]]).exact().real[1].value.toString(30));
teach.solveSystem([[2, 1], [1, 3]], [1, 2]).steps.map((s) => s.title)
```
